report:
### Conclusion
The claim that prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks causes dangerous carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) buildup is **false**.

### Evidence and Findings
* **Gas Diffusion:** Carbon dioxide molecules are microscopic gas particles that pass freely through the breathable, porous material of cloth and surgical face masks. While masks trap larger respiratory droplets, they do not impede gas exchange.
* **Clinical Studies:** A study published in the *Annals of the American Thoracic Society* evaluated blood gas levels in both healthy individuals and patients with severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). Researchers found no clinically significant changes in oxygen or $\text{CO}_2$ levels during mask use, even during physical exertion.
* **Expert Guidance:** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and major medical institutions affirm that wearing cloth or surgical masks does not cause hypercapnia ($\text{CO}_2$ toxicity) or hypoxia (oxygen deprivation). Healthcare personnel have worn surgical masks for long procedures for decades without experiencing adverse blood-gas issues.
* **Perceived Discomfort:** Sensations of warmth, humidity, or air restriction while wearing a mask are related to thermal comfort and minor breathing resistance, not a dangerous buildup of exhaled gases.

### Sources
* Annals of the American Thoracic Society: https://www.atsjournals.org/doi/abs/10.1513/AnnalsATS.202007-812RL?role=tab
* USA Today Fact Check: https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/
* Michigan Medicine: https://www.michiganmedicine.org/health-lab/4-mask-myths-put-you-risk
* UW Medicine: https://rightasrain.uwmedicine.org/well/prevention/face-mask-myths
